faq.q: Which similarity metrics does it compute?
faq.a: Six per comparison: Levenshtein edit-distance similarity, Jaro-Winkler (prefix-weighted, good for names), Jaccard word-set overlap, Cosine on word-frequency vectors, the Dice coefficient, and the longest common substring reported in characters. The headline percentage is the average of the five ratio metrics, but if both Jaccard and Cosine are zero (no shared words) the overall score is pulled down so unrelated texts aren't labelled 'somewhat similar' from shared letters.

faq.q: How is the Fuzzy Match tab different from the main Similarity tab?
faq.a: Fuzzy Match is for short strings like names, addresses, or product codes. It blends Jaro-Winkler and Levenshtein similarity (case-insensitive) into one score and gives a clear MATCH or NO MATCH against a threshold you set with a slider (default 80%). It also shows the raw edit-distance count. The main tab is for longer passages and adds shared-passage highlighting, word analysis, and a statistics table.

faq.q: Can I compare many pairs at once?
faq.a: Yes, use the Batch CSV tab. Paste one string pair per line separated by a delimiter you choose (pipe, comma, tab, or semicolon), set a threshold, and Compare List produces a table with each pair's similarity and a match/no-match result, plus a count of how many matched. Lines missing a delimiter are flagged. Download CSV exports the results as batch-similarity.csv.

faq.q: Is this a plagiarism checker, and does it do line-by-line diffs?
faq.a: It measures similarity between two texts you supply and can highlight shared word sequences and the longest common substring, which helps spot copied passages, but it doesn't search the web. For a git-style, line-by-line view of exactly what changed, the page points you to the separate Diff Checker tool. Your texts and comparison history stay in your browser; it keeps the last 10 comparisons as similarity figures, not full text.
